lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Saturday. The shift is over. The headset is off.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The apartment doesn't quite know what to do with you. Neither do you.

choices.label: Sleep until the city forgets you.
Coffee by the window. Watch the street.
Replay this week's calls in your head.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The kettle clicks. Somewhere in your skull, this week's calls replay anyway.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Same street names. Same careful voices. A pattern, if you squint.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your phone buzzes. Coworkers, a bar, tonight, question mark.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You send it and set the phone face-down. Small mercy.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The afternoon burns off slow. Laundry. A walk you don't remember taking.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Evening comes anyway. The notebook sits on the desk, patient as a lawyer.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Outside: the whole city, off the clock. Inside: you, alone with the pattern.

beats.prompt: Alone with the pattern. What do you do?

choices.label: Start a private life — dates, go outside, everything.
I should focus on what happened.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You close the laptop, untie the necktie, pour a drink.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Off duty. The pattern can wait. Patterns always say they'll wait.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You open the notebook and write down everything you remember.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Street names. Times. The careful voices. It fills three pages too easily.
